measurement_description: The paper does not measure anything related to faith or religion. It evaluates the effectiveness of a fairness-constrained training procedure (MinDiff) for deep neural networks, particularly in the over-parameterized regime, focusing on fairness metrics like Equality of Opportunity (measured by False Negative Rate gap) based on non-religious sensitive attributes (e.g., gender on the CelebA dataset).
